blocks.orig: Mwanza is a port city on the shore of Lake Victoria, in north-western Tanzania. It is the busiest and second largest city after Dar Es Salaam. Since it is located on Lake Victoria, the fishing industry is an important part of the economy. On the lake itself you can see the beautiful Bismarck Rock in the water; a very impressive scene. The Bismarck Rock is Mwanza’s icon and is a precariously balanced boulder atop the lovely jumble of rocks in the lake next to the Kamanga ferry pier. Hence Mwanza’s nickname “Rock City”.
blocks.html: On the shore of Lake Victoria in north-western Tanzania lies Mwanza, a port city that is the country’s busiest and second largest after Dar Es Salaam. Thanks to its position on Lake Victoria, fishing is a major part of the local economy. Out on the water you can admire the beautiful Bismarck Rock, a truly striking sight. This icon of Mwanza is a boulder balanced precariously on top of a lovely cluster of rocks in the lake, beside the Kamanga ferry pier. It is the reason Mwanza carries the nickname “Rock City”.

blocks.orig: In Mwanza’s town center are colonial buildings like the crumbling hilltop Dr. Robert Koch’s House. The 1935 Indian Public Library, mosques and Hindu temples reflect Indian influence. And the Makoroboi area is full of shops.
blocks.html: The town centre of Mwanza contains colonial buildings such as the crumbling Dr. Robert Koch’s House on the hilltop. Indian influence shows in the Indian Public Library of 1935, the mosques and the Hindu temples, while the Makoroboi area is packed with shops.

blocks.orig: Mwanza is surrounded by hills strewn with enormous boulders. Despite its rapidly rising skyline, Mwanza manages to retain a casual feel. In addition to being a stop on the way to Rubondo Island National Park, Mwanza is a great starting or finishing point to or from safaris through the Serengeti.
blocks.html: Hills scattered with huge boulders surround Mwanza. Even with its fast-growing skyline, the city keeps a relaxed atmosphere. Besides being a stopover on the way to Rubondo Island National Park, Mwanza makes an excellent place to begin or end a safari through the Serengeti.

blocks.orig: Lake Victoria was named after Queen Victoria by the explorer John Hanning Speke and with a surface area of approximately 59,947 km², Lake Victoria is Africa’s largest lake by area, the world’s largest tropical lake, and the world’s second largest fresh water lake by surface area. The lake has a maximum depth of between 80 and 84 metres. The lake includes many species of fish that appear nowhere else, especially cichlids. Invasive fish, such as the Nile perch, have driven many endemic species to extinction.
blocks.html: The explorer John Hanning Speke named Lake Victoria after Queen Victoria. Covering roughly 59,947 km², it is the largest lake in Africa by area, the largest tropical lake in the world and the second largest freshwater lake on earth by surface area. Its maximum depth lies between 80 and 84 metres. Many fish species found nowhere else live in the lake, cichlids in particular, although invasive fish such as the Nile perch have pushed numerous endemic species to extinction.

blocks.orig: On Lake Victoria are two island national parks: Rubondo Island National Park and Saanane Island National Park.
blocks.html: Two island national parks lie in Lake Victoria: Rubondo Island National Park and Saanane Island National Park.

blocks.orig: Rubondo Island National Park is one of two Tanzanian national parks on an island. It is located in the south-western corner of Lake Victoria, about 150 km west of Mwanza. The main island, Rubondo is 237 km2 in size and the habitat is mixed evergreen and semideciduous forest. Rubondo Island became a game reserve in 1965, to provide a sanctuary for animals and is uninhabited. It can be reached by park boat and accommodation on the island includes the park bandas.
blocks.html: Rubondo Island National Park is one of only two Tanzanian national parks situated on an island. You find it in the south-western corner of Lake Victoria, some 150 km west of Mwanza. Rubondo, the main island, covers 237 km2 and its habitat is a mix of evergreen and semideciduous forest. The island has been uninhabited since it was declared a game reserve in 1965 to serve as a sanctuary for wildlife. A park boat takes you across, and the park bandas are among the places to stay on the island.

blocks.orig: Rubondo Island boasts a number of the indigenous species such as hippo, bushbuck, vervet, sitatunga, crocodiles, elephants, chimpanzee, giraffe, black and white colobus monkeys, suni and grey parrots, buffalos, bushpig, hyrax, warthog and large spotted genet cat.
blocks.html: Among the indigenous species living on Rubondo Island are hippo, bushbuck, vervet, sitatunga, crocodiles, elephants, chimpanzee, giraffe, black and white colobus monkeys, suni and grey parrots, buffalos, bushpig, hyrax, warthog and the large spotted genet cat.

blocks.orig: Mwanza can be reached by car from the Serengeti national park in 5 hrs. It is also served by a regional airport.
blocks.html: By car, Mwanza is a 5 hrs drive from the Serengeti national park. The city also has a regional airport.

blocks.orig: Travel Tips from our experts about Mwanza

My name is Edgar and I am a guide in Mwanza for 11 years. Our really enjoy Mwanza as it offers something for everyone’s taste. One can relax on the waterfront and watch the famous Bismarck Rock or go on a sightseeing trip to old town. I get many guest coming here after safari and some continue to Rubondo Island national park.
blocks.html: I am Edgar, and I have worked as a guide in Mwanza for 11 years. Our guests really like Mwanza because there is something here for every taste. You can unwind on the waterfront and look out at the famous Bismarck Rock, or take a sightseeing tour through the old town. Many guests arrive here after their safari, and some travel on to Rubondo Island national park.

blocks.orig: How long to stay? 2 days is best to see the city
blocks.html: How long should you stay? 2 days is ideal for seeing the city

blocks.orig: Mwanza is the busiest and second largest city after Dar Es Salaam. It is located at Lake Victoria where you can see the beautiful Bismarck Rock in the water – Mwanza’s famous landmark. Mwanza’s town center has many historical buildings and shops. It is also a great stop on the way to Rubondo Island National Park, or as a finishing point from safari.
blocks.html: After Dar Es Salaam, Mwanza is the busiest and second largest city in Tanzania. It sits on Lake Victoria, where the beautiful Bismarck Rock rises from the water as Mwanza’s famous landmark. The town centre is full of historic buildings and shops. Mwanza is also a handy stop en route to Rubondo Island National Park, or a place to end your safari.
the Mwanza region has a population of 1,135,878 people
